ConocoPhillips inched up 0.28% today after two days of recovery from a sharp 2.9% drop on November 23rd. That sell-off followed the collapse of climate talks at COP31, where governments rejected a draft deal that failed to commit to phasing out fossil fuels—a development that briefly weighed on oil majors. Today's modest gain reflects stabilization as oil markets steadied: US crude holding at $82 per barrel with Brent at $91.80, and the immediate shock from the climate summit disappointment has faded.

The stock remains down 2% over two weeks, sitting at the lower end of its recent range, which suggests investors are still pricing in some caution around long-term demand pressures and regulatory uncertainty despite this week's rebound. Meanwhile, geopolitical disruptions—Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries and U.S. efforts to acquire Russian assets outside Russia—are adding complexity to global energy markets without yet translating into a clear directional push for the stock.
